params.body:
## Why

Two small, unrelated things on the settings screen.

**The RealGarant password travelled to the browser, and saving the pane deleted it.** The input in
the warranty pane was rendered with the stored value as its `value=`, and that stored value is the
*encrypted* password: the ciphertext reached every browser that opened the pane, and came back on
every save. The field was `disabled` when a password was set, which is what kept the round trip from
re-encrypting it, but disabled is a browser convention, not a guard, and it hid a second problem:
an empty submit deleted the row (`updateCreateSetting` deletes on a blank value). That is the state
the form is in the moment the reset button has been clicked, and the state anyone is in who opens the
pane with the field enabled and saves without retyping.

**The LYRA toggle was a blank tile.** `Access::showChat()` was true for every BEHEERDER whatever
`CHATBOT_ENABLED` said. On an environment with the chatbot off that put a floating round button
bottom-right of every screen, with nothing behind it but the 404 `ChatBotController` aborts with, and
with the theme's `fa-comments` glyph purged out of the build it rendered as an empty square, on top
of the save row of the settings form.

## What

**Warranty password**

- The pane renders an empty password field (`x-ui.password`, which has `value=""` built in). The
  stored value never leaves the server, in ciphertext or otherwise.
- An empty submit keeps what is stored: `updateWarranty` drops `warranty_password` from the data it
  writes when nothing was typed, instead of writing a blank and deleting the row. A typed value is
  encrypted and stored exactly as before.
- A muted hint under the field says which of the two states you are in:
  "Er is een wachtwoord ingesteld. Laat leeg om het te behouden." / "Nog geen wachtwoord ingesteld."
  It uses the `help` slot of `x-ui.field` (`ui-field-help`), the same hint the other panes use.
- The field is not `disabled` any more: it is empty and typeable, which is what the hint promises.
- Nothing changed about what RealGarant receives. `RealGarantService` still reads the same row and
  still decrypts it; the only change is when that row is written.

**Chat toggle**

- `Access::showChat()` is now `!Auth::guest() && config('variable.chatbot.enabled')`. That is the one
  condition the whole app already used (the layout's include, the Echo client, the abort in
  `ChatBotController`), so what is shown and what answers cannot disagree.
- The button gets `aria-label` / `title` from `trans('chatbot.toggle')`, plus `aria-expanded` and
  `aria-controls`, and `chatbot-app.js` keeps `aria-expanded` in step with open/close.
- The glyph is an inline SVG instead of a Font Awesome class, so a purged theme sheet cannot turn it
  back into a blank square. A focus ring was added.
- `body { padding-bottom: 6rem; }` in the chatbot's own scoped style block, so the page can scroll
  past the corner the button floats over. It sat on top of the settings save row.

## What the reset button does

**Today (before this PR):** `onclick="$('#warranty-password').removeAttr('disabled'); $('#warranty-password').val('')"`.
It only enables and empties the input. The clearing itself was a side effect of the save path:
an empty `warranty_password` reached `updateCreateSetting`, which deletes a setting whose value is
blank. So the button did not clear anything by itself, and neither did it have to: *any* empty submit
cleared the password, which is the bug in A.

**After this PR:** clearing is explicit. The button toggles an Alpine `reset` flag, which flips a
hidden `warranty_password_reset` field from `0` to `1`, marks the input read-only and shows a line
saying the password will be cleared on save (the button becomes a Cancel). The controller clears the
row only on that flag. So the button keeps doing exactly what it was for — the way to remove a stored
password — and it is now the *only* thing that does it. `warranty_password_reset` is deliberately not
in `UpdateWarrantyRequest::rules()`: it is a command, not a setting, and keeping it out of
`validated()` keeps it out of the loop that writes every validated field to the settings table.

## Checked

The same pattern elsewhere, as asked:

- `nederlandMobiel_api_key` — nothing left. Its pane went away with the platform credentials
  (#256); the key only survives as a fallback lookup in `App\Support\IntegrationCredentials`, in
  `CUTOVER.md` and in tests. It is never rendered into an input. The replacement pane
  (`_tabs/koppelingen.blade.php`) reports "ingesteld" and never a value.
- `warranty_password` is the **only** encrypted setting that was echoed into an input. It is also the
  only `encrypt()` in a settings path at all — the other `encrypt` calls in `app/` are
  `ApiHelper::encrypt` on record ids in API resources.
- Two other credential inputs do echo their stored value, but neither is encrypted, so neither is in
  the class of bug this PR fixes. Reporting them rather than touching them:
  - `resources/views/settings/dealer/_tabs/carpass.blade.php` renders
    `<input type="password" name="carpass_password" value="{{ $dealer->carpass_password }}">` — a
    plaintext column on `dealers`, sent to the browser in the clear on every open of that pane.
  - `resources/views/settings/setting/_tabs/removebg.blade.php` renders the remove.bg `api_key` the
    same way (plaintext setting).

Verification: `php artisan view:cache` plus `php -l` on the two compiled views; `php -l` on every
changed PHP file; `StylesheetSyntaxTest`, `UiApiUsageTest`, `BuildContractTest` and
`ClassReferencesResolveTest` pass locally. No CSS changed, so no build. The database-backed tests
(`WarrantyPasswordTest`, `ChatToggleTest`, `SmokeTest`) could not run on this machine — the local
MySQL only answers to a socket login this session does not have — so CI is the judge there.

New tests: `tests/Feature/WarrantyPasswordTest.php` (the pane never contains the stored ciphertext or
the password; the hint matches the state; an empty submit and a missing field both keep the row; a
typed password is stored encrypted; the reset flag is what clears it) and
`tests/Feature/ChatToggleTest.php` (no toggle when the chatbot is off, a labelled toggle when it is
on, and a 404 on the endpoint when it is off).
params.title: Settings: the warranty password stays server-side, the chat button only when LYRA is on
